items.title: Facilities Operations Monthly Review - Minutes, June 2026
items.section: June 2026 discussion of the Tower B plumbing backlog
items.content:
Nolan Achterberg reported a growing plumbing work order backlog in North Campus Tower B since March, primarily sensor flush valves, mixing valves, and medical gas outlet repairs on inpatient units, including the ICUs. Most of the aged Tower B plumbing work orders are on hold in "Awaiting Parts" status for Aqualine SV-200 solenoid modules and MedGuard MG-4 O2 outlet latch assemblies ordered from ACME Mechanical Supply. Several patient rooms have been taken out of service pending parts. Nolan noted that under the prior Great Lakes Plumbing Supply agreement these parts were pulled from the consignment cage the same day, and that Facilities was not consulted on the Exhibit B specialty item list in the ACME agreement before it was signed.

Tobias Lund (Supply Chain) stated that the ACME delays are **temporary**, attributed to a manufacturer allocation issue at Aqualine and to ACME establishing new manufacturer accounts. Supply Chain expects lead times to normalize by the end of the summer. The first ACME quarterly business review was held in May 2026; Supply Chain reported that fill rate reporting by Exhibit was not yet available from ACME at that time.

Charlotte Engel (Nursing) reported that out-of-service rooms in Tower B are affecting patient flow and ED boarding, and asked for estimated return-to-service dates for each room.

items.title: Lakeshore Health Campus and Building Facilities Reference
items.section: Tower B specialty parts supply and storage history
items.content: From the Tower B opening in 2019 until February 2026, specialty repair parts for Tower B fixtures were supplied by Great Lakes Plumbing Supply under a consignment arrangement, with consignment stock held on-site in the North Campus Central Plant storeroom (see Great Lakes Plumbing Supply agreement LH-SC-2019-044). Effective 2026-02-24, plumbing parts are supplied by ACME Mechanical Supply under agreement LH-SC-2026-017. Supply Chain is the owner of vendor agreements; Facilities Operations is the owner of fixture standards. Technicians should consult the current supply agreement for lead times before committing a repair date to a nursing unit.

items.title: Facilities Operations Monthly Review - Minutes, September 2026
items.section: September 2026 after-hours General Maintenance plumbing callbacks
items.content:
Wendell Ruiz reported that overnight General Maintenance callouts for plumbing issues have continued to rise each month since April. Most are P2 Urgent calls for toilets and flush valves, mixing valves, and medical gas outlets on Tower B inpatient units. Under SOP FAC-OPS-014 Rev 4, these calls route to the GM on-call first; GM technicians are not licensed for flushometer or sensor valve, medical gas, or backflow repair, so they make the area safe and the ticket is reassigned to a plumber at the start of the next day shift. Charge nurses have reported repeated overnight visits to the same room without repair. Charlotte Engel noted that Nursing understood from prior practice (Rev 3) that P2 plumbing calls would page the on-call plumber.

Action item AI-2026-06-04 (review effect of SOP FAC-OPS-014 Rev 4 on after-hours plumbing response and completion times) remains **open**. The review has not started because the General Maintenance Supervisor position was covered on an interim basis in July and August. Corinne Ashby noted the review must also consider the FY26 overtime reduction target of 18%.

items.title: Lakeshore Health Campus and Building Facilities Reference
items.section: Tower B specialty plumbing fixture standard
items.content:
The following specialty fixtures were specified by the Tower B design team and installed throughout North Campus Tower B:

- **Aqualine SV-200 sensor flush valves** on every patient and staff toilet. The SV-200 uses a proprietary solenoid module and diaphragm kit; there is no generic or cross-manufacturer substitute.
- **Aqualine sensor faucets** at hand hygiene sinks, using a model-specific sensor faucet solenoid.
- **ThermaMix TMV-50 thermostatic mixing valves** controlling hot water delivery temperature at point-of-use and unit-level locations. These valves are part of the Lakeshore water management program for Legionella control.
- **MedGuard MG-4 medical gas zone valve boxes** and MedGuard MG-4 headwall outlets for oxygen, medical air, and vacuum. The O2 outlet latch assembly is model-specific to the MG-4 outlet body.
- **Reduced pressure zone (RPZ) backflow preventers** at domestic water, process water, and equipment connections, serviced with manufacturer RPZ backflow repair kits and relief valve assemblies.

Repair parts for these Tower B fixtures are not stocked by general building supply distributors and are not interchangeable with the commodity parts used in other buildings.

items.title: Lakeshore Health Campus and Building Facilities Reference
items.section: Commodity plumbing fixtures in other Lakeshore buildings
items.content: All Lakeshore buildings other than Tower B use standard commodity plumbing fixtures: manual or standard-diaphragm flushometers, conventional two-handle or single-lever faucets with generic cartridges, and standard medical gas outlets from multiple manufacturers installed during various renovations. Parts for these fixtures are carried in campus shop stock and are available from most plumbing distributors, typically same-day or next-day. Tower A (1972) and Riverside Hospital (1965) have the oldest piping systems and the highest rate of leak and drain work orders, but their parts are commodity items.
